source_checks.finding: Fetched at the address returned by search (same article as the cited en-us address). The iPhone steps are confirmed: open Settings and tap your name, tap Sign-In & Security, tap Change Password, follow the onscreen instructions, then choose Remove Other Devices or Keep All Devices Signed In. Exact excerpt confirmed: 'The easiest and most secure way to change your Apple Account password is to use your iPhone or another trusted device'. The one-hour wait sentence ('You might be required to wait one hour before changing your Apple Account password.') is also on the page. Applies to this iPhone user.

Introduction confirms the exact excerpt: 'change your Apple Account password immediately and ensure that two-factor authentication is enabled.' The 'Watch for these signs' section says: 'Apple will never ask you to log in to any website, or to tap Accept in the two-factor authentication dialog, or to provide your password, device passcode, or two-factor authentication code or to enter it into any website.' The passage wording is a close paraphrase of this and is supported. Applies to any Apple Account.

The Android steps are on this page: open Settings, tap Google, your name, Manage your Google Account, Tap Security & sign-in, under 'How you sign in to Google' tap Password, then Enter your new password and tap Change Password. The page is for Android phones, so this does not apply to this iPhone user and is correctly unused. The excerpt 'If you change or reset your password, you'll be signed out everywhere except:' is in the same article.

required_actions.action: Change the Apple Account password now, since a password was typed on a fake website
Make sure two-factor authentication is turned on
Use the iPhone Settings route: Settings, tap your name, Sign-In & Security, Change Password, then complete the prompts
Choose Remove Other Devices or Keep All Devices Signed In for other signed-in devices
Know that Apple never asks for your password or a two-factor code on a website
Possible one-hour wait before the password can be changed

The over-limit wording is confirmed in the separate 'Learn how attachments work in Gmail' section: Gmail automatically removes the attachment and adds it as a Google Drive link in the email. Applies to Gmail in a browser on a computer, as the user has.

required_actions.action: Open Gmail in the browser
Start a new message with Compose
Select the Attach icon at the bottom of the compose window
Choose the files and confirm with the Open button
Personal account limit of 25 MB, with a Google Drive link when the total is over the limit
